publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: apps/nickstire/server/cron/jobs/crossSellOutreach.ts is the cron in this diff, and the change to it is COMMENT-ONLY — an operator gate block documenting what must be decided before `sms_cross_sell_outreach` is enabled. No control flow in the cron changed. The behavioural change is one layer down, in the scorer the cron reads from, and is covered by server/affinityScoring.test.ts (15). FAIL-CLOSED, non-operator path: this cron has no operator in the loop, so the relevant property is that it cannot send when its own gate is unreadable. featureFlags.isEnabled() ends in `catch { return false }` — an unreadable flag disables the loop rather than enabling it — and `sms_cross_sell_outreach` is off, so the cron sends nothing either way. CROSS-LOOP FAIL-CLOSED (new, and the reason this diff touches the cron at all): declinedWorkRecovery.ts contacts the same customers about the same open estimates and sends with `skipPersist: true`, so cross-sell's COOLDOWN_DAYS could never have observed one of its sends. The affinity query now EXCLUDES any estimate the recovery loop has claimed (any followUp*AttemptedAt set), so recovery owns an estimate the moment it touches it and the double-text is impossible by construction rather than unlikely by cooldown. Separately, server/loopShapeContract.test.ts (16) replays this exact cron's production history: a run that succeeds while producing nothing is now classified `dormant`, and a run that succeeds without MEASURING its output is `unknown`, never healthy — the shape that let cross_sell report `completed` daily from May to July while sending zero (ROS-033). NOT production-verified: no v3 prediction has been computed anywhere, and the flag stays off. Volume risk is documented at the gate — 2-hour tier, 12 runs/day x MAX_SMS_PER_RUN 10.

capability-ledger-updated.ref: capability-ledger.json: NEW capability `sms-customer-identity` (Inbound SMS customer identity resolution + consent), at codeState merged / operationalState unit_verified / exposure disabled. The first version of this diff filed the evidence under `content-governor` — the CADENCE governor, whose capability is creation reservations and publish-door enforcement. An SMS identity/consent test proves nothing about it, and because this JSON generates REALITY-LEDGER.md it would have made the governor's verification history misleading. Caught in review on #1149; the misfiled entry was removed rather than left alongside. THE DEFECT: loadCustomerContext matched on LIKE '%'+last-10-digits with .limit(1) and no ORDER BY, so a shared household line, business number or recycled number resolved to a non-deterministic row. #988 feeds that row's name and vehicle into the drafter, and CONFIRM / CANCEL / estimate-approval replies MUTATE the booking, lead, callback and estimate selected by the same shared phone — the disclosure was the visible half, the mutation was the worse one. THE FIX: ambiguity refuses EVERY phone-linked facet. Asymmetric on purpose — identity and history withheld, `optOutOnAnyMatch` carries the most restrictive opt-out across all matches and survives, so a disclosure fix cannot become a consent regression. Send-time opt-out in server/sms.ts is phone-keyed and independent (ROS-025), so this is defence in depth. P2 BLOCKER RECORDED, not hidden: the multi-match FREQUENCY in production is unmeasured. The log.warn makes it observable; no number exists yet; ROS-079 stays unranked. Phone-ownership validation is listed as deferred scope because a household line on a SINGLE row produces the same disclosure and no query over `customers` can see it.
